audit_metadata.audit_type: Security audit and compliance scanning for production systems

findings.title: API Key Present in .env File
findings.description: An Anthropic API key is present in llm-mesh/.env file. While the file is correctly gitignored and has never been committed, having real credentials in the repository poses risk if the gitignore is modified or if developers inadvertently share the file.
findings.recommendation:
1. Rotate the exposed API key immediately
2. Use environment variables loaded from secure vault (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault)
3. Add pre-commit hooks to prevent secrets from being committed
4. Consider using .env.local for machine-specific secrets

findings.title: Dashboard API Key Not Configured
findings.description: The dashboard/.env file has API_KEY commented out with a note that authentication will show warnings but still allow access in development mode. This is acceptable for development but must be configured for production.
findings.recommendation:
1. Ensure API_KEY is always set in production environments
2. Add startup validation that fails if API_KEY is not set in production mode
3. Document required environment variables for production deployment

findings.title: Child Process and Exec Usage
findings.description: Multiple files use child_process/exec functions. While the dashboard security utilities implement safe patterns (shell: false), other usages should be reviewed.
findings.recommendation:
1. Audit all exec/spawn calls to ensure shell: false is used
2. Use the security.js safeExec() wrapper for all command execution
3. Add input validation for all command arguments

findings.title: innerHTML Usage in Coverage Reports
findings.description: The coverage report files (coverage/sorter.js, coverage/prettify.js) use innerHTML. These are auto-generated test coverage files and pose minimal risk but should be noted.
findings.evidence: innerHTML usage found in generated coverage files
findings.recommendation: These are auto-generated test coverage files - no immediate action required. Ensure coverage reports are not served in production.

findings.title: Hardcoded Test Credentials
findings.description: Test files contain hardcoded credentials like 'secret123' and 'key-abc'. These are test fixtures and pose no security risk as they're not used in production.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable for test fixtures. Consider adding comments to clarify these are test-only values.

positive_findings.title: No Vulnerable Dependencies
positive_findings.description: npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities across 311 dependencies (7 production, 305 dev)

positive_findings.title: .env Files Properly Gitignored
positive_findings.description: Both llm-mesh/.env and dashboard/.env are in .gitignore and have never been committed to git history

positive_findings.title: Safe Command Execution Utilities
positive_findings.description: dashboard/server/utils/security.js implements secure patterns: shell: false, path validation, error sanitization, and timeout handling

positive_findings.title: LLM Safety Filters Enabled
positive_findings.description: The llm-mesh configuration has PII, injection, and secrets filters enabled (SAFETY_ENABLE_PII_FILTER, SAFETY_ENABLE_INJECTION_FILTER, SAFETY_ENABLE_SECRETS_FILTER)

compliance_summary.notes: Full compliance audit requires manual code review and penetration testing

recommendations_priority.action: Rotate the Anthropic API key in llm-mesh/.env
Add startup validation for required production environment variables
Implement pre-commit hooks to scan for secrets
Audit all exec/child_process calls for injection vulnerabilities

next_steps: Schedule follow-up security review in 30 days
Consider implementing secret scanning in CI/CD pipeline
Document security requirements for production deployment
